potential_retrieval_noise.representation_excerpt: reducing sleep duration by 120 minutes for six consecutive nights

potential_retrieval_noise.raw_fact_or_missing_context: First 7 window days had sleep durations 357-368 min; baseline mean was 480.9 min. The actual mean reduction for those 7 days is ~117 min, not 120 min for 6 nights.

potential_retrieval_noise.representation_excerpt: reducing sleep duration by 59 minutes for six consecutive nights
potential_retrieval_noise.possible_mechanism: Conflation of aggregate and per-night statistics: the model likely retrieved the overall period mean difference (-59.2 min) and incorrectly applied it as the per-night reduction during the disrupted block.
potential_retrieval_noise.raw_fact_or_missing_context: The -59 min figure is the comparison of 28-day baseline mean to 14-day window mean, not the per-night reduction during the delayed-onset phase which was ~117 min below baseline.

potential_retrieval_noise.raw_fact_or_missing_context: The first 7 nights averaged 363.4 min, not 422 min. The 422 min value is the full 14-day window mean.
